component.name: FILES (SYSTEM, READ-ONLY)
component.description:
What it does Reads, writes, lists and deletes files in your organization's file storage - the same files people see in the Files area of the app - so an orchestration can load its inputs and save what it produces.

How it works Each node runs one operation, chosen in the Inspector, on a path such as reports/q3.csv. READ_FILE emits the file as a file artifact; READ_DIRECTORY emits each file in a folder, up to 100. WRITE_FILE saves the incoming file, or the Content text when no file arrives, as a new version if the file exists. WRITE_DIRECTORY saves every incoming file into a folder. LIST lists a folder and DELETE moves a file or folder to the trash. The path can be filled from the incoming data with ${field} placeholders. A path that does not exist fails the run - nothing is quietly written to the root instead.

Configure
- Operation - READ_FILE, READ_DIRECTORY, WRITE_FILE, WRITE_DIRECTORY, LIST or DELETE.
- File Path - the file or folder to act on; empty means the root for LIST and the folder operations.
- Content - the text WRITE_FILE writes when no file arrives.

In and out In: optional files to write, and any data the placeholders use. Out: the files read, plus the incoming data with the operation, the path, file_count and the files read, written or listed.

Use it when
- An orchestration starts from a document or spreadsheet someone uploaded.
- You want to save a generated report, export or image for people to open.
- A pipeline should process every file in a folder.

component.manifest_yaml:
extension_type: agent
name: Files
description: >
  Runs one operation on the organization's files - read a file or a folder's
  files, write a file or a set of files, list a folder, or delete a file or
  folder. A path that does not exist fails the run; nothing is ever written
  anywhere the path did not name.

input_ports:
  - port_name: input
    port_type: in
    # WRITE_FILE writes the incoming file when there is one, else Content;
    # WRITE_DIRECTORY writes every incoming file. The other operations ignore
    # the artifact, so a file or nothing is accepted.
    artifact_type_input: optional(file)
    # READ_FILE emits the file, READ_DIRECTORY each file it read; the other
    # operations emit no artifact.
    artifact_type_output: optional(file)
    multi_artifact: true
    # The incoming request_data is forwarded, with the operation's result on top.
    response_data_passthrough: request_data
    response_data:
      operation: string - The operation that ran.
      path: string - The path acted on, with its placeholders filled.
      file_count: integer - Files read, written or listed; 0 for DELETE.
      files: array (optional) - The entries read, written or listed - id, name, type (file or folder) and size in bytes. Not set by DELETE.

input_parameters:
  - name: operation
    type: select
    label: Operation
    options: [READ_FILE, READ_DIRECTORY, WRITE_FILE, WRITE_DIRECTORY, LIST, DELETE]
    default: READ_FILE
    required: true
    description: The file operation this node runs.
  - name: path
    type: text
    label: File Path
    default: "${file_path}"
    description: The path from the root of the organization's files, such as reports/q3.csv. A folder for READ_DIRECTORY, WRITE_DIRECTORY and LIST, where empty means the root. Accepts ${field} placeholders.
  - name: content
    type: text_long
    label: Content
    default: ""
    description: The text WRITE_FILE writes when no file arrives. Accepts ${field} placeholders.
    depends_on:
      parameter: operation
      visible_when: [WRITE_FILE]

path.description: The path acted on, with its placeholders filled.

file_count.description: Files read, written or listed; 0 for DELETE.

files.description: The entries read, written or listed - id, name, type (file or folder) and size in bytes. Not set by DELETE.
